name: Business Owner Residence Card (Autorisation d'Établissement)

requirements.blocker_text: A foreign national pursuing independent/self-employed business activity (as opposed to employer-sponsored work) must obtain an 'autorisation d'établissement', requiring business registration, a NINEA tax number, and proof of sufficient financial resources. Standard employer-sponsored work permits do not cover freelance or self-employment activity.
requirements.fix_path: Register the business, obtain a NINEA tax number, and demonstrate sufficient financial resources to secure the autorisation d'établissement.

outcome.duration_length: not specified precisely in the sources reviewed

sources.title: Expat.com (private expatriate-guide site) -- confirms the 'autorisation d'établissement' as the distinct route for self-employed/independent business activity, separate from the employer-sponsored work permit, requiring business registration, a NINEA number, and proof of financial resources

DLA Piper Africa (GENI & KEBE Lawyers) -- describes Senegal's updated Investment Code, which reduced the eligibility threshold for small/very-small enterprises to CFA 15,000,000 (roughly USD 25,000, not independently converted/verified) to qualify for investment incentives, applied under a stated principle of equal treatment for domestic and foreign investors

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Senegal). STATUS: DRAFT -- both sources are private (tier 4 and tier 3); Senegal's own investment authority (APIX) and Investment Code text could not be fetched directly in this build (APIX's site returned a connection timeout, and UNCTAD's hosted Investment Code page returned a 403 error). IMPORTANT SCOPING CAVEAT: this route models the general 'autorisation d'établissement' residence mechanism for self-employed/business-owning foreigners, NOT a dedicated investor-visa or golden-visa product -- no source reviewed in this build confirmed that Investment Code registration (the CFA 15,000,000 threshold) itself grants or is a precondition for any residence permit; that connection was deliberately NOT asserted to avoid overstating a link the sources don't establish. The CFA 15,000,000 Investment Code threshold is included as related context on Senegal's investment-incentive regime, not as a qualifying condition of this specific route.
